subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a public normal-chat tool-error delivery policy beyond `messages.suppressToolErrors`, and what should happen when a mutating tool fails but the assistant final reply sounds successful?
rationale: Source inspection confirms the UX gap, but choosing `all | final | off` semantics changes public config and failed-side-effect visibility safety, so automation cannot safely decide the product contract.

options.title: Add explicit opt-in delivery policy
options.body: Define a default-compatible enum such as `all | final | off` that preserves current warnings by default while allowing hosted or group-chat operators to opt into final-only or off behavior with focused tests.

options.title: Keep boolean-only policy
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported all-off escape hatch and document that OpenClaw will not add a success-aware enum for now.

options.title: Move policy to channels
options.body: Let team-chat plugins own warning visibility where channel UX differs, avoiding another global message config key.

recommendation.title: Add explicit opt-in delivery policy
recommendation.body: Define a default-compatible enum such as `all | final | off` that preserves current warnings by default while allowing hosted or group-chat operators to opt into final-only or off behavior with focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest inspected history on the current failed-tool warning policy and authored the merged related PR that explicitly left this broader issue open.
